messages:
Maya (VP Product): Thanks for the session today. A couple of follow-ups folks asked for in product: 1) how tightly should we bind roadmap choices to the market thesis vs short-term revenue, 2) a one-sentence answer the sales team can use about our "moat" vs infra/cloud vendors, and 3) guidance on when to fast-track integrations vs build in-house.

Jordan (CEO): Short answers: 1) roadmap should be market-led with revenue signals tipping priority; prioritize features that increase net retention and reduce time-to-value. 2) Moat line: we combine a high-throughput, unified runtime with developer-friendly ops and transparent unit economics — so customers get production-grade inference without rebuilding ops. 3) Integrations: fast-track for platforms that unlock >$1M ARR or strategic channel reach; otherwise prefer composable primitives.

Carlos (Head of Sales): For playbook: what's the ten-second objection response when prospects say "we can just use cloud provider X"? Need something crisp.

Jordan (CEO): Use: "Cloud providers are great for experiments; Redwood makes production predictable and economical — same API across hosted, reserved, and private with clear cost levers and SLA-backed ops. If you care about unit economics and uptime at scale, that difference matters."

Nora (Research): Can we include a benchmark claim? Sales likes numbers. Maybe "10-30% cost reduction" or similar? Any guardrails?

Jordan (CEO): Benchmarks ok but be conservative. Use phrasing like: "Customers typically see meaningful cost and latency improvements through batching, caching, and quantization — ask us for workload-specific benchmarks." Leave exact percentages for case studies vetted by Research & Sales.

Devin (SRE): Operationally: if we push Hosted optimizations that change request behavior (e.g., more aggressive batching), what's the message for Dedicated/Private customers? We can't surprise them.

Maya (VP Product): Good point. Rule: upstream runtime improvements are default unless they affect API compatibility or determinism. For Dedicated/Private, ship opt-in flags for any behavior that could alter output timing or token accounting and document in release notes.

Carlos (Head of Sales): Signal for Dedicated outreach? Last time we used spend thresholds; should we add model usage patterns (e.g., heavy embedding traffic) as triggers?

Jordan (CEO): Primary signal = sustained spend above working threshold ($25k/mo placeholder) OR sustained resource hotspots (peak QPS, embedding throughput) OR regulatory/security requirement. Add embedding-heavy workloads as a secondary signal. RevOps to formalize thresholds.

Nora (Research): For messaging about open model catalog: can we say "vendor-agnostic model catalog"? Want to ensure legal doesn't flag anything about third-party models.

Maya (VP Product): Use "model-agnostic catalog" in public docs, and internal phrasing can say "curated open models + vendor-neutral integrations." Legal review for public claims.

Devin (SRE): Action items for infra: I'll draft a compatibility policy for Hosted runtime changes and an opt-in flag plan for Dedicated/Private by next Wed.

Carlos (Head of Sales): I'll add Jordan's objection-response and the Dedicated signals to the sales playbook this afternoon and loop RevOps.

Maya (VP Product): I'll update the roadmap doc to reflect market-led prioritization and add a column for "revenue signal" that ties features to net retention impact.

AllHandsBot: Recording and notes uploaded: https://redwood.internal/recordings/2365209999 
Jordan (CEO): Thanks everyone  keep follow-ups here or DM Maya.
